items.item: A timeout bounds how long a client holds its own resources waiting on a call, measured directly against a real slow endpoint versus a real fast one on the same client-side timeout.

items.item: Deadline propagation shares one absolute deadline down a call chain rather than resetting a fresh timeout at every hop, so a later hop can see that the time is already gone and skip work nobody will collect.

at.step: Reveal: deadline propagation through a call chain

items.item: Capped exponential backoff slows every client down by the same schedule, which is why it still produces correlated clusters of retries rather than spreading them out.

items.item: Jitter is the specific fix for correlated retry clustering, confirmed both by a real client retrying against a real flaky server and by a direct simulation contrasting a hundred synchronized clients with and without it.

items.item: A retry budget caps how many times a process is allowed to retry in total, independent of any single call's own backoff schedule — once exhausted, the client fails fast rather than retrying forever.

items.item: A circuit breaker's Open state measurably fails in microseconds because it stops calling the dependency at all, not because the call itself got faster.

at.step: Reveal: a circuit breaker fails fast

items.item: A circuit breaker's Half-Open state sends a limited trial request rather than immediately trusting the dependency is healthy again; a failed trial reopens the breaker.

at.step: Reveal: a circuit breaker fails fast

items.item: An idempotency key's dedup guarantee is about the server's own effect count, not just about the client seeing the same response text back.

at.step: Reveal: an idempotency key, deduplicated for real

items.item: A retry budget and a circuit breaker solve different problems: a budget caps a single client's own total retry volume; a breaker stops an entire dependency from being called at all once it looks unhealthy.
Retrying at every layer of a multi-hop stack multiplies load geometrically, which is why the sourced best practice is to retry at a single point in the stack rather than at each hop independently.

items.item: An idempotency key only makes a retry safe if the client actually reuses the same key on its retry; generating a fresh key per attempt defeats the whole mechanism.
